speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Shipston. Down. You have had your ten miles of being a sack, and the sack is over.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not glad of it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: You were glad at the fifth mile, and you are glad now, and you may go on saying you are not. The nag believes the sitting, not the sentence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The back liked the sitting. I am allowed to dislike being ordered into a liking.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Dislike it on your feet, then. From here you walk. The pace is the horses', two and a half miles in the hour, and for a back that complains when it sits too long and complains when it stands too long, that pace is exactly right.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will walk it. I will not thank the pace until I have hated it for an hour and found it still right.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Oats at Shipston, a penny the peck over last month. I asked, because I feed six horses and a spare, and a penny is how a harvest introduces itself.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A penny the peck. I am not buying oats. I am hearing them.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Hear them, then. Hay is not to be had. Not at a price I will say in a street, and not at a price I will pay. The horses will eat what the road still has, and the road is thinner than it was in July.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we bait on what you already carry, and we do not make a market out of a stop.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Bread, and a drink, and the horses' noses in what I brought for them. Twenty-one miles today, all told. You have done ten of them sitting. The rest are yours.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Chipping Norton for the night. I know the distance. I do not know the bed, and I am not going to pretend a bed is a comfort before I have seen it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: An inn, and a supper, and a bed you will share. Fourteen pence, if the house is the house it was last month. If it is more, I will say so before you sit.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The rise after this. The old stones are on the right. I said I would not turn, and I am saying it where the road can hear it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: You will see them and you will keep walking. I have led strings past those stones in rain and in dry, and the stones have never once come down to the road to help with a load.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good. I have had enough of things that ask to be looked at. The pack stays on your saddle. I am walking empty, as ordered.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Empty, and at my pace. If you stride out to prove the back is mended, I will put you up again, and you may be not-glad for another ten.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will keep your pace. The back is not mended. It is only better going than it was on a bench in Stratford, and that is a low boast.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: A low boast is the kind that arrives. Drink. Then we go. I am not paying a penny a peck extra so that you can make a speech over a trough.
